key_insight: Scale weight decay by the current learning rate fraction so regularization fades as training cools, preserving optimization behavior while avoiding the steady norm shrinkage caused by constant decoupled weight decay.
engineering_relevance: For large-scale neural network training, this simple change can speed convergence without changing the optimizer’s target, making it attractive for practical pretraining pipelines.
method: Replace constant decoupled weight decay with weight decay scaled by η/η_max.
Prove asymptotic stationarity is preserved for both SGD and Muon.
Use steady-state analysis to explain why weight norms stabilize instead of continuously shrinking.
evidence_signal: In mixture-of-experts training, Muon-SW reached the same validation loss 30% faster at the largest scale across models from 72M to 930M parameters, trained at about 600 tokens per active parameter.
watch_item: The reported gains come from large-scale MoE pretraining, so results may depend on model class, training schedule, and the exact learning-rate/decay setup.
paper_title: Scale Weight Decay and Train Better
